title: Address PR #119 feature parser review
description: Review feedback on PR #119 for loreweaver-0m9.5.18: make feature parsing table-driven for grant levels and feature identity, avoid splitting option subheadings, and add feature coverage guards. Done means accepted feedback is implemented with RED/GREEN evidence, importer tests pass, and PR branch is updated.
close_reason: All PR #119 review feedback evaluated, implemented, and verified; child tasks closed with evidence.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Review evaluation: item 1 accepted. Current parseFeatures reads level from leading prose and defaults to 1, but bead design explicitly says class features often require progression-table name->level mapping. This can emit incorrect feature.data.level. Item 2 accepted. Current broad title-case heuristic can split option subheadings inside feature bodies because it treats any matching title-case line after a feature as a new feature. Item 3 accepted. runImporter currently wires features without any coverage guard, unlike creatures/classes/subclasses. Suggested direction accepted with scope: parse progression tables from the Classes slice into grant-level anchors, use those anchors as the primary feature identity/level source, and keep prose lead-ins as fallback/validation for subclass features and fixtures where no table anchor is present.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: RED verification: npx vitest run packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseFeatures.test.ts packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/pipeline.test.ts -> exit 1 as expected. Failures show current parser promotes class-table headers and option subheadings as features, defaults no-table Second Wind to level 1, does not use table level for Action Surge, and runImporter writes packs with 0 features / ignores minFeatureCount.
